trigger: Boone's back door, Act III (trader). Some of his filters are expired.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The yard's half empty. Boone is thinner, still smiling. 'Prices went up. Everything went up. Except morale.'

nodes.speaker: trader_boone
nodes.text: Filters. Twelve. Fresh off the truck. For whiskey, fuel, or that nice rifle.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You turn one over. Lot number, date: expired three years ago. Half the box is the same.

nodes.speaker: trader_boone
nodes.text: ...Okay. Okay! Half are good. I'll sort them. Don't tell anybody. Please.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Ruiz gets word to the yard. By morning, Boone's gone. Kessler made an example. His stock is in a ditch.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You get what's left. You don't feel good about it.

nodes.speaker: trader_boone
nodes.text: Thank you. Seriously. You're a good guy. Rarest thing in the yard.

nodes.speaker: trader_boone
nodes.text: Kessler knows everything. Kessler also needs somebody to trade for his cigarettes.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Behind you, the yard's floodlights flicker. Fuel's running low there too.
